Ready for the maintainer to merge (clean). Built and tested locally at head `89ab6519`, trial-merged with main `d54580ca`. The PR stays a draft until the maintainer flags it ready.

## What looks good

- **Exactness holds by construction.** The Y-slab query walks the same directed edges (`a = pts[i]`, `b = pts[(i+1)%n]`), uses the same half-open rule `p.y >= ylo && p.y < yhi`, and computes `x_at = a.x + (q.y - a.y) * (b.x - a.x) / (b.y - a.y)` with the same operand order as `Loop::contains_xy` (`crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs:143-148`). The inner re-check at `slice_index.rs:139` means a slab bug can only cost a compare, never move a verdict.
- **The slab proof is sound.** An edge `[ylo, yhi)` lands in slab `k` exactly when `q.y` is in `[ylo, yhi)`. So the index reads exactly the edges the full scan toggles, and XOR parity does not depend on order. Non-finite `q.y` and NaN-bounded edges fall out with the same no-crossing result.
- **Every plane and every sample stay.** `rest.rs` caches `Rc<IndexedSlice>`. `islands_at` still returns the region (law (c) reads it) and `island_holds` asks the index. The levels-only `cut_planes.rs` is gone, and `reach.rs` is byte-identical to main.
- **File and law hygiene.** No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. Every index is bounds-safe (`get`, `min(slabs)`, `saturating_sub(1)`). Files stay under 400 lines (slice_index 231, rest 273, reach_tests 213). Provenance line present. No new dependency. The decision file records the accepted and the rejected design.

## The three exactness questions

1. **Same membership for every point: yes.** Same `x_at` expression, same operand order, same half-open test, same per-edge toggle. The only change is that the index touches only the edges that cross `q.y`; the slab proof shows that set is exactly the edges the full scan toggles.
2. **`ramp_at(500, 36.0)` moves 274-292 (the 19 part-true `ShankHit` the levels-only set lost): covered.** `reach_tests::a_many_plane_ramp...` runs `assert_same("wall ramp 500", ramp_at(500, 36.0))`. That asserts the indexed law equals the all-plane reference (`band_reach_reference`) on the whole findings vector, in order. The reference convicts those moves, so any subset loss turns the assert red. It does not name 274-292, but equality to the reference that convicts them is the stronger guard.
3. **Sensitivity: confirmed.** The direct pin is a differential test against `Region::contains` as the oracle, so it fails on any superset or subset. I mutated the index in my worktree (`q.x < x_at` -> `q.x < x_at + 1.0`, a superset) and the pin went red at `Point2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }` (index `false`, Region `true`); I then reverted it. The law pins are also mutation-sensitive: `assert_eq!(new, old)` catches both directions, and the stepped fixture additionally requires a `ShankHit { part: true }` to be present (the exact subset the wide-only variant dropped). There is no separate fault-injection harness in the PR, but the exact-equality checks turn red on a superset or a subset of the covered fixtures.

## Results (locally, worktree `cc-pr3620-review`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3`)

- Trial merge with `origin/main` (`d54580ca`): clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib verify::`: 160 passed, 0 failed. Key pins ok: `slice_index::tests::the_index_equals_region_contains_bit_for_bit`; `reach_tests::a_many_plane_ramp_reads_only_the_samples_near_its_discs` (`ramp_at(500,36)` and the stepped fixture); `reach_tests::indexed_band_reach_keeps_every_finding_of_the_pooled_scan`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Targeted tests

- Example catalog: no post or toolpath change, not run.
- Light lane: not run. Its twins are motion and app lanes that do not read the verifier.
- Heavy: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches `app heavy: every target` and `motion heavy: every target` (the full cut-tier lanes). This review did not re-run the heavy lane. A `P2` gets no heavy step, and AGENTS.md says no PR is owed heavy. The author ran the targeted `app heavy: verify` lane (450 s), named in the body. It is not re-run here, so it is not an independent pass.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The stepped fixture uses `ramp_at(500, 49.0)`. The narrow upper block's Y 45 wall is 4 mm off that path, which is the wall the levels-only set lost. This is the right shape.
- The PR is still a draft. Flag it ready, then merge. Do not merge a draft.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
